label: this-tree
rule: the dead letter stores the bytes that were owed at quarantine time — a snapshot, not a fact
the journal row is the fact: seal, payload and accounts can all move while a letter waits
push already rebuilt the body from the row (deliver_events reads events_after); only the replay read the freeze
one fact, one verdict per surface: the same seq must reach a consumer as the same body whichever command delivers it

faces.claim: the replayed body carries the seal the JOURNAL holds for that event (not the seal the quarantine froze)
faces.note: the chain unmade the tx between quarantine and replay; push delivered the retraction to t1 first: true; the replay then sent seal="reverted" (frozen body said "finalized"), exit 0

faces.claim: replay and push answer the SAME event with the SAME body — a fresh target read through `push` receives what the replayed target receives
faces.note: one journal, two surfaces: push built its body from the row (seal "reverted"), the replay sent the freeze (seal "reverted")

faces.claim: the replay report names the letters whose body came from the journal instead of the freeze (`rebuilt`)
an UNCHANGED letter still replays byte-for-byte (the documented signature guarantee where it is true)
a letter with no journal row replays its STORED bytes and exits 0 — nothing is ever dropped
a replay refused again stays pending and exits 3 (the queue keeps holding it)
